previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A 50-year-old male with a history of dilated non-ischemic cardiomyopathy, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation on warfarin, prior strokes, type II diabetes, and morbid obesity was admitted for acute on chronic systolic heart failure exacerbation presenting with worsening shortness of breath, orthopnea, and lower extremity edema. The exacerbation was attributed to high dietary salt intake and intermittent noncompliance with diuretic therapy. He was treated with 160 mg of IV furosemide over two days, resulting in clinical improvement with reduced edema and weight loss from 139 kg to 128.7 kg. His heart function remained stable with an ejection fraction of 30%, and no acute ischemia was noted. Chronic issues including bilateral foot ulcers, blepharitis, and obstructive sleep apnea were monitored, with no signs of infection in the wounds. He was discharged home on his prior medications, including torsemide 60 mg twice daily, with instructions for strict low-salt diet, daily weight monitoring, and follow-up for cardiac MRI, podiatry, and ophthalmology.

Brief Hospital Course:
Mr. ___ is a ___ yo M with PMH notable for atrial 
fibrillation/atrial flutter (CHADS2 of 5) on coumadin, dilated 
cardiomyopathy with recent exacerbation of systolic CHF ___ 
on echo from ___, DM, HLD, and hx. of previous multiple CVAs 
who is admitted for a GI bleed and found to have colonic mass on 
colonoscopy with no evidence of metastases on CT scan. Patient 
was initially admitted to the ICU for concern of rapid bleeding 
from lower source. He was supported with IVF and when his Hct 
remained stable, he was transferred to the floor. Colonoscopy 
and EGD were performed and he was found to have a colonic mass 
in the descending colon concerning for malignancy; superficial 
biopsy revealed high grade dysplasia. There were also scattered 
polyps throughout the colon but these were not removed due to 
concern for bleeding in the context of patient's elevated INR. 
CT scan did not show definitive evidence of mestastasis. After 
discussion of risks and benefits, the patient elected to undergo 
surgical resection of the mass during this admission. 

As such, he was medically optimized for surgery with the help of 
cardiology in the following ways: his warfarin was stopped on 
admission and when his INR was less than 2 he was started on a 
heparin drip, which was stopped 4 hours prior to surgery. For 
his CHF, his torsemide, ramipril metalazone were all held on 
admission due to concern for bleeding. His diuretics were 
restarted the day before surgery and then held the day of 
surgery. His metoprolol was fractionated to tartrate and 
continued the day of surgery. His ramipril was held throughout 
admission due to low systolic blood pressures. 

Patient was taken to the operating room on ___ where he 
underwent a laparoscopic sigmoid colectomy. The procedure was 
uncomplicated; please see operative report for further details. 
The patient was admitted to the Colorectal Surgery service for 
standard post-op care. 

Per pathway, patient's diet was advanced starting POD1 from 
clears and was tolerating a regular diet on POD2. He received 
Dilaudid PCA for pain control initially and transitioned to oral 
analgesics once tolerating oral intake. Patient's systolics 
ranged from ___ to low 100s. He did have a couple of episodes of 
hypotension with systolics to the ___ that responded with 
albumin boluses. He also had very brief, asymptomatic, and 
self-resolving runs of V-tach. 

Anticoagulation was resumed on POD2 with his home dose of 
Coumadin and heparin gtt bridge. He reached therapeutic on his 
INR on POD4. Per Cardiology, his home metoprolol and torsemide 
were restarted on POD2, ramipril on POD3, and spironolactone on 
POD4. Patient was instructed to restart metolazone on POD5 (day 
after discharge). His cardiac status remained stable throughout 
the hospital course.

Patient was medically ready for discharge on POD4. At time of 
discharge, he was tolerating a regular diet, voiding freely, 
passing flatus and stool, and ambulating independently. Labs on 
day of discharge did show hypokalemia and he was repleted.  
Patient was offered ___ services but declined. He was discharged 
home in good condition.

Discharge Instructions:
Dear Mr. ___,

You were admitted to ___ for a GI bleed and found to have a 
mass in your colon concerning for cancer. There were other 
polyps seen in your colon as well for which you will need to 
undergo another colonoscopy with Dr. ___ in ___. 
You have done well and are now ready for discharge home. 
Multiple follow up appointments were made for you to see your 
healthcare providers, and it is important for you to keep these. 
You also need labs (INR, electrolytes) drawn on ___ 
___ and have the results faxed to Dr. ___ Dr. 
___. 

In regards to your COLON SURGERY, samples from your colon were 
taken and this tissue has been sent to the pathology department 
for analysis. You will receive these pathology results at your 
follow-up appointment. If there is an urgent need for the 
surgeon to contact you regarding these results they will contact 
you before this time. You have tolerated a regular diet, are 
passing gas and your pain is controlled with pain medications by 
mouth. You may return home to finish your recovery.

Please monitor your bowel function closely. You may or may not 
have had a bowel movement prior to your discharge which is 
acceptable, however it is important that you have a bowel 
movement in the next ___ days. After anesthesia it is not 
uncommon for patients to have some decrease in bowel function 
but you should not have prolonged constipation. Some loose stool 
and passing of small amounts of dark, old appearing blood are 
expected. However, if you notice that you are passing bright red 
blood with bowel movements or having loose stool without 
improvement please call the office or go to the emergency room 
if the symptoms are severe. If you are taking narcotic pain 
medications there is a risk that you will have some 
constipation. Please take an over the counter stool softener 
such as Colace, and if the symptoms do not improve call the 
office. If you have any of the following symptoms please call 
the office for advice or go to the emergency room if severe: 
increasing abdominal distension, increasing abdominal pain, 
nausea, vomiting, inability to tolerate food or liquids, 
prolonged loose stool, or extended constipation.

You have ___ laparoscopic surgical incisions on your abdomen 
which are closed with internal sutures and a skin glue called 
Dermabond. These are healing well however it is important that 
you monitor these areas for signs and symptoms of infection 
including: increasing redness of the incision lines, 
white/green/yellow/malodorous drainage, increased pain at the 
incision, increased warmth of the skin at the incision, or 
swelling of the area. Please call the office if you develop any 
of these symptoms or a fever. You may go to the emergency room 
if your symptoms are severe.

You may shower; pat the incisions dry with a towel, do not rub. 
The small incisions may be left open to the air. If closed with 
steri-strips (little white adhesive strips) instead of 
Dermabond, these will fall off over time, please do not remove 
them. Please no baths or swimming for 6 weeks after surgery 
unless told otherwise by your surgical team.

You will be prescribed a small amount of the pain medication 
oxycodone. Please take this medication exactly as prescribed. 
You may take Tylenol as recommended for pain. Please do not take 
more than 3000mg of Tylenol daily. Do not drink alcohol while 
taking narcotic pain medication or Tylenol. Please do not drive 
a car while taking narcotic pain medication.

No heavy lifting greater than 6 lbs for until your first 
post-operative visit after surgery. Please no strenuous activity 
until this time unless instructed otherwise by Dr. ___.

In regards to your HEART FAILURE, weigh yourself every morning, 
call your PCP if weight goes up more than 3 lbs. Please also 
take your cardiac medications.

In regards to your ATRIAL FIBRILLATION, please continue to take 
Coumadin at your usual dose. You need your INR checked on 
___ please let your ___ know of these results 
so your dosage can be adjusted accordingly.

Thank you for allowing us to participate in your care! Our hope 
is that you will have a quick return to your life and usual 
activities. Good luck!

ABDOMEN:

HEPATOBILIARY: The liver demonstrates homogenous attenuation throughout. 
There is no evidence of focal lesions. There is no evidence of intrahepatic or
extrahepatic biliary dilatation. The gallbladder is within normal limits,
without stones or gallbladder wall thickening.
PANCREAS: The pancreas has normal attenuation throughout, without evidence of

stranding.
SPLEEN: The spleen shows normal size and attenuation throughout, without
evidence of focal lesions.
ADRENALS: The right and left adrenal glands are normal in size and shape.
URINARY: The kidneys are of normal and symmetric size with normal nephrogram. 
There is no evidence of stones, focal renal lesions, or hydronephrosis. There
are no urothelial lesions in the kidneys or ureters. There is no perinephric
abnormality.
GASTROINTESTINAL: Small bowel loops demonstrate normal caliber, wall thickness
and enhancement throughout. There is colonic diverticulosis.  Surrounding the
distal descending colon, there is fat stranding and tiny adjacent lymph nodes
measuring up to 6 mm (series 3, image 99) without significant wall thickening
or obvious mass ( 3:100). Appendix contains air, has normal caliber without
evidence of fat stranding. There is no evidence of mesenteric lymphadenopathy.
RETROPERITONEUM: There is no evidence of retroperitoneal lymphadenopathy.
VASCULAR: There is no abdominal aortic aneurysm. There is moderate calcium
burden in the abdominal aorta and great abdominal arteries.

PELVIS: The urinary bladder and distal ureters are unremarkable. There is no
evidence of pelvic or inguinal lymphadenopathy. There is no free fluid in the
pelvis.

REPRODUCTIVE ORGANS: Reproductive organs are within normal limits.

BONES AND SOFT TISSUES:

There is depression of the anterior endplate of L5 with no obvious surrounding
inflammatory changes to suggest an acute fracture, therefore this is likely
remote.  There is no suspicious bone lesion.
Abdominal and pelvic wall is within normal limits.
